 Muthoot FinCorp Forex and Remittance: RBI Scope, KYC, Costs, GST and TCS 
 By 
 CA Sandeep Kanoi 
 Finance 
 Articles 
 November 20, 2026 
 Share: 
 Summary: Muthoot FinCorp Limited appears in the Reserve Bank of India’s Kochi regional list of Authorised Dealer Category-II entities, with its registered office at Muthoot Centre, Punnen Road, Thiruvananthapuram and listed authorised branches. Its Muthoot FinCorp ONE platform describes foreign-currency purchase and sale, forex cards and outward remittances for specified non-trade current-account purposes. AD-II status is narrower than unrestricted permission for every foreign-exchange activity: the customer, purpose, amount, branch, payment route and documents must fall within FEMA and RBI directions. The service literature allows online or branch-based KYC for relevant products and states that rates, currency availability and some service costs are transaction-dependent. Current statutory tax rules also matter. GST applies to the taxable value of money-changing services under rule 32 , while TCS under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme generally uses a ₹10 lakh annual threshold; from 1 April 2026, the rate for education and medical remittances is 2%, while other LRS purposes generally remain at 20%, subject to exceptions. This profile separates authorised remittance and travel-forex services from offshore leveraged forex or CFD trading , which it neither describes nor endorses.

 Muthoot FinCorp Legal Entity and RBI Authorisation
 The verified contracting entity for this profile is Muthoot FinCorp Limited, not an overseas broker and not merely a brand name. The RBI’s Kochi regional AD Category-II list identifies Muthoot FinCorp Limited at Muthoot Centre, Punnen Road, Thiruvananthapuram and enumerates authorised branches. The list was current to October 2026 and includes branch additions dated 3 August 2026. AD-II authorisation permits specified non-trade current-account transactions and money-changing activities. It does not by itself authorise leveraged online forex speculation , contracts for difference, unrestricted capital-account transfers or every service at every location.
 Question 
 Verified position 
 Customer consequence 
 Who is the entity? 
 Muthoot FinCorp Limited 
 Confirm that order, invoice and payment instructions name the authorised entity or a disclosed executing partner. 
 What is the RBI category? 
 Authorised Dealer Category II 
 Use only permitted money-changing and specified non-trade remittance purposes. 
 What is the customer channel? 
 Muthoot FinCorp ONE and listed branches 
 Digital initiation does not remove KYC, purpose or branch-availability checks. 
 Is it an offshore forex broker? 
 No such role is established by the reviewed sources 
 Do not use the service description as authority for CFDs, margin trading or overseas margin remittances . 
 AD-II scope in practical terms
 RBI directions permit AD-II entities to release or remit foreign exchange for enumerated non-trade purposes such as private visits, business travel, conferences and specialised training, medical treatment abroad, overseas education, examination fees, employment processing, emigration, visa fees and certain international subscriptions. The exact purpose code and supporting evidence remain decisive. A service page listing a purpose is not approval of an individual transaction, and the authorised dealer may decline or seek enhanced due diligence.
 Customer Services and Permitted Use Cases
 The Muthoot FinCorp ONE forex pages describe purchase and sale of foreign currency, outward remittance, reloadable multi-currency forex cards and branch or digital initiation. Cash collection or sale of currency generally requires a branch visit, while a card order or remittance may begin online. Currency availability is expressly subject to market liquidity. Card issuance or servicing can involve a disclosed product partner; a customer should identify the issuer, money changer, executing authorised dealer and platform operator separately on the order and invoice.

 What the profile does not establish
 Nothing in the reviewed authorisation establishes permission for a resident to send money abroad as margin or a margin call for speculative forex trading . RBI guidance requires permitted electronic forex transactions to use an authorised electronic trading platform or a recognised Indian stock exchange under the applicable rules. Absence from the RBI Alert List would not prove authorisation. Customers should not present a different purpose, split transactions to bypass controls or use another person’s LRS entitlement .
 KYC Documents, Quote and Transaction Process
 Customer and purpose verification
 The platform describes video KYC or branch verification for relevant forex services. A transaction can require PAN, identity and address evidence, passport and visa, travel tickets, admission or fee documents, medical papers, employment or emigration records, beneficiary bank information, source-of-funds evidence and a completed purpose declaration. Requirements vary by product and risk. An authorised dealer must perform customer due diligence, sanctions screening and FEMA purpose checks and may ask for additional records.
 Rate and cost confirmation
 The customer should obtain a written quote showing the base or reference rate, provider mark-up or spread, service charge, card or delivery charge, correspondent-bank deduction, beneficiary-bank charge, applicable GST, TCS and the amount expected to reach the beneficiary. Rates are time-sensitive and may expire. The provider’s rate-lock terms state that a fixed-rate order can produce a partial refund or forfeiture if cancelled or not completed, depending on the loss and published conditions. Transaction-specific terms should be reviewed before paying.

 How it should be checked

 Read the invoice and product schedule 
 Product, location and payment channel may change the charge.

 Ask whether charges are OUR, SHA or BEN and confirm final receivable amount

 Check taxable value and invoice treatment under CGST rule 32

 Aggregate eligible LRS remittances across authorised dealers for the financial year

 Settlement, Cancellation, Refund and Grievance Route
 Settlement timing depends on cut-off, completion of KYC and source-of-funds review, payment clearance, beneficiary-bank details, currency liquidity, correspondent routing and sanctions screening. A promised processing estimate should be documented, but it is not the same as an unconditional beneficiary credit time. Incorrect beneficiary details can cause rejection, return, delay or extra charges. The customer should retain the order number, rate confirmation, invoice, Form A2 or purpose declaration, bank debit proof, SWIFT or remittance reference and beneficiary confirmation.
 For cancellation, the platform terms state that a no-obligation order cannot be cancelled after execution and that a failed or cancelled fixed-rate order may lead to partial refund or forfeiture depending on the affiliate money changer’s loss. Customers should ask where a refund will be credited, what deductions can apply and the expected timeline. The published help channel is 1800-102-1616 and [email protected] . A complaint should first identify the order, entity, branch, payment and requested remedy. If unresolved, the customer can use the applicable RBI complaint channel after following the regulated entity’s internal process, while card-specific complaints may also need the issuer or product partner.
 GST and TCS on Foreign Exchange and Remittance
 GST valuation is applied to the service value
 Under CGST rule 32 , the value of money-changing service can be computed from the difference between the buying or selling rate and the RBI reference rate multiplied by currency units, subject to special rules where a reference rate is unavailable. The supplier may instead choose the optional slab-based deemed valuation method for the financial year. GST at the applicable rate is charged on that taxable service value and taxable service charges, not automatically on the entire foreign-currency principal. The invoice should show the method and tax amount.
 LRS TCS after the 2026 rate change
 For remittance under LRS , section 206C(1G) generally uses an aggregate ₹10 lakh threshold for the resident buyer in a financial year. From 1 April 2026, TCS on amounts above the threshold is generally 2% for education or medical treatment and 20% for other purposes. A remittance for education financed by a qualifying loan under section 80E is excluded under the statutory rule. TCS is collected by the authorised dealer and is a tax credit, not necessarily the customer’s final tax liability. The customer should disclose prior-year remittances accurately and reconcile the certificate, Form 26AS and income-tax return.
 A provider web page can retain an older threshold or rate after the law changes. Current statutory material should therefore prevail over an outdated FAQ. Overseas tour-package TCS is a separate rule and should not be merged with the LRS remittance calculation. Business remittances, non-residents and non-LRS transactions can follow different provisions.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Is Muthoot FinCorp Limited currently listed as an RBI AD-II entity?
 Yes. The RBI Kochi regional AD-II list reviewed for this article names Muthoot FinCorp Limited and lists authorised branches, with 2026 updates.
 Does AD-II status permit every kind of forex transaction?
 No. It permits specified non-trade current-account remittances and money-changing activities within RBI directions. It does not establish blanket authority for every product or purpose.
 Can a resident use LRS to remit margin for offshore forex trading?
 No. RBI guidance does not permit LRS remittances for overseas forex-trading margins or margin calls .
 Which KYC papers can be required?
 PAN, identity and address proof, passport and visa, purpose evidence, beneficiary bank details, source-of-funds records and Form A2 or another declaration may be required.
 Is GST charged on the full amount of foreign currency bought?
 GST applies to the taxable value of the money-changing service determined under rule 32 and to taxable charges. It is not automatically 18% of the currency principal.
 What LRS TCS rates apply from 1 April 2026?
 Subject to the ₹10 lakh annual threshold and exceptions, the general rate is 2% for education or medical remittance and 20% for other LRS purposes.
 Where should a customer first raise a complaint?
 Use Muthoot FinCorp’s published customer-care channel with the order and remedy sought, then follow the regulated entity’s escalation and applicable RBI complaint process if unresolved.
 Key Takeaways
 Muthoot FinCorp Limited is listed by RBI as an AD Category-II entity ; the authority is purpose- and service-specific.
 The verified service scope covers travel forex, outward remittance and related products, not offshore leveraged forex or CFDs .
 A written quote should separate rate, spread, charges, GST, TCS, correspondent deductions and beneficiary amount.
 KYC, purpose, source-of-funds and beneficiary checks remain mandatory even when the order begins online.
 Current tax law prevails over any provider FAQ that retains an older TCS threshold or rate.

 Disclaimer: This article is a factual educational profile of Muthoot FinCorp Limited’s stated forex and remittance services and its RBI AD Category-II listing, checked from primary materials available on 20 November 2026. It is not legal, FEMA, banking, tax, GST, accounting, travel, immigration, consumer-dispute, investment or trading advice and does not recommend Muthoot FinCorp, any card issuer or partner, any remittance, currency, exchange rate, rate lock or service. AD-II authorisation has a defined scope and does not prove that every branch, platform feature, currency, amount, customer, beneficiary or purpose is currently available or permitted. Product partners, execution roles, exchange rates, spreads, fees, card charges, delivery coverage, correspondent deductions, cut-offs, documents, cancellation terms, refund timing, GST valuation, LRS thresholds and TCS rates can change. The executing authorised entity may reject, delay, return or request more information for a transaction, and an overseas correspondent or beneficiary bank may impose deductions or compliance holds. Residents must not use LRS for prohibited transactions , including overseas forex-trading margins or margin calls, misstate a purpose, split remittances to avoid controls, use another person’s entitlement or conceal beneficial ownership. Provider webpages can contain older tax information; readers must verify current RBI directions, the exact contracting and executing entities, the written quote and invoice, purpose code, source of funds, beneficiary details, live tax law and applicable complaint route .
